title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Card Catalog. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Card Catalog
options.lineage: library card catalogs, drawers and ruled index cards
options.thesis: Every project, role, tool and certificate is a filed record; scrolling is flipping through the drawer.
options.viewport: Navin's author card set huge on cool white stock: name as the main entry, role and school as subject lines, the red index rule on top, race and email actions on the card's foot, drawer tabs down the right edge as the scroll rail.
options.risk: Tips into library kitsch if typewriter faces or cream paper creep in; it has to stay crisp, modern and cool-toned.

raised.raise: Every record sits on one 12-column grid with fixed row heights, so the catalog reads as measured, not decorated.
Scroll position is the one axis: a single progress value drives the drawer rail, the pinned card flip and the active tab together.
Rank comes from tonal and size steps, never from extra boxes: no container nests inside a card.
Total colour commitment: the red index rule is the only hue on the site, used at one weight.
Text bands to fixed course heights, so every record row shares one baseline rhythm.

options.label: The Line
options.lineage: Manila LRT/MRT line maps and transit wayfinding
options.thesis: The portfolio is one transit line; sections are stations and your scroll is the train.
options.viewport: A thick green line drops from the name down the left; the next stations are labeled ahead, and a dot rides the line as you scroll.
options.risk: Familiar: vertical-timeline portfolios are common, so it lives or dies on how strictly the signage system is held.

options.label: Title Card Wall
options.thesis: Projects, roles and certificates as rows of title cards; the focused one grows and tells you what it is.
options.viewport: Navin as the featured title over a dimmed wall, with a Projects row already peeking in sideways below.
options.case: Recruiters recognise it instantly (holds audience identification), but most projects have no artwork, so tiles would be empty posters (loses clarity).
options.risk: Without real poster art per project it reads as a skeleton of a streaming app.

options.label: Session Sleeve
options.thesis: Each section as a sleeve: duotone portrait cropped hard, name at an angle, one flat colour field.
options.viewport: Portrait cropped to one corner, the name across a flat orange field at an angle.
options.case: Loud and retro against a pinned modern-minimal brief; loses both axes.
options.kept: Total colour commitment: one hue, used with full conviction.

options.label: Deep Dive
options.thesis: Scroll as descent, every section at a depth.
options.viewport: Surface at the name, the page darkening with depth.
options.case: Atmospheric but says nothing about front-end work; loses both axes.
options.kept: One scroll axis drives every state change together.

options.label: Cracktro Scroller
options.thesis: Bitmap text riding baselines over a black void.
options.viewport: One ivory line of text over drifting starfields.
options.case: Lands in the dark-terminal rut; loses both axes.
options.kept: Rank by tonal step, never by enclosing boxes.

options.label: Signal Bench
options.thesis: Content measured against a ten-division graticule.
options.viewport: A phosphor trace across the name.
options.case: An instrument costume; loses both axes for a recruiter audience.
options.kept: Everything measured against one strict grid.

options.label: Coiled Earth
options.thesis: The page rises in coils, each a course of content.
options.viewport: Banded clay courses with the name stamped in.
options.case: Warm craft material with no tie to software work; loses both axes.
options.kept: Every line banded to a fixed course height.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean minimal developer portfolio, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Large name and one-line intro, a nav top-right, selected work below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from thousands of other portfolios by design.
